name: Product Management
certifications: Optional: Scrum.org Professional Scrum Product Owner (PSPO I)
tools: Product analytics such as Amplitude, Mixpanel or Google Analytics

beginner.summary: For aspiring and new product managers, business analysts and engineers moving into product roles. Covers the product manager's role, understanding customers and their problems, interviews, market analysis, vision and value propositions, problem statements, requirements and user stories, prioritisation, roadmaps, working with engineering and design, product metrics and analytics, experiments, launches, stakeholders, agile delivery, pricing and the everyday tools of the job.
prerequisites: Works in or near software, digital or product teams
Comfortable with spreadsheets and basic data
Curious about customers and business outcomes
outcomes: Discover customer problems through interviews and research
Write problem statements, requirements and user stories teams can build from
Prioritise work and build an outcome-based roadmap
Define product metrics, read analytics and plan a feature launch

days.topic: Product Management Overview: The Role, the Product Lifecycle and Course Setup
subtopics: What product managers do and do not do
Product, project and programme management compared
The product lifecycle from idea to retirement
Working with engineering, design and business
Types of product roles: B2C, B2B, platform and internal
Product management in Indian and global companies
A week in the life of a product manager
Course project: choosing a product to work on
days.lab_task: Pick a real product for the course project, fill in a one-page product canvas, compare product and project management responsibilities for that product and rate your skills baseline.
days.deliverable: Product canvas, role comparison and skills baseline
checks: The canvas names users, problem, value and business model
Product and project responsibilities are separated correctly
The baseline covers discovery, delivery, data and communication

days.topic: Understanding Customers: Problems, Jobs to Be Done and Personas
days.lab_task: Write jobs-to-be-done statements, two proto-personas and an empathy map for your course product, and list the assumptions you will test in interviews.
days.deliverable: Jobs statements, personas, empathy map and assumption list
checks: Each job states situation, motivation and outcome
Personas describe goals and pains, not only demographics
At least five testable assumptions are listed

days.topic: Customer Interviews: Planning, Asking and Synthesising
subtopics: Taking notes and recording with consent
days.lab_task: Run three short customer interviews about your course product, synthesise the notes with an affinity map and present the top three insights with quotes.
days.deliverable: Interview guide, notes, affinity map and insight summary
checks: Questions ask about past behaviour, not hypothetical wishes
Insights are grouped from notes across interviews
Each insight has at least one supporting quote

days.topic: Market and Competitor Analysis
subtopics: Market size: TAM, SAM and SOM
days.lab_task: Estimate the market for your course product, map four competitors on a positioning map and write a one-page market summary with opportunities.
days.deliverable: Market estimate, positioning map and market summary
checks: TAM, SAM and SOM are estimated with stated assumptions
Competitors are positioned on two meaningful dimensions
The summary names at least two opportunities

days.topic: Product Vision and Value Proposition
subtopics: What a product vision is for
Vision compared with strategy and roadmap
Keeping the vision stable while plans change
days.lab_task: Write a product vision and a value proposition canvas for your course product, give a sixty-second pitch to the class and revise based on their questions.
days.deliverable: Vision statement, value proposition canvas and pitch
checks: The vision helps decide between two sample features
The canvas links product features to customer pains and gains
The pitch states customer, problem and difference in sixty seconds

days.topic: Defining Problems Before Solutions: Opportunity Statements
subtopics: Size and urgency of a problem
Choosing which problem to solve first
days.lab_task: Turn five feature requests into problem statements, gather evidence for each from your interviews and data, and choose the problem to solve first with reasons.
days.deliverable: Five problem statements with evidence and a chosen problem
checks: Each request becomes a problem statement without a solution
The chosen problem is justified by size and urgency

days.topic: Writing Product Requirements: PRDs, User Stories and Acceptance Criteria
subtopics: What a requirements document is for
User stories and the INVEST criteria
days.lab_task: Write a one-page PRD for the chosen problem, break it into user stories with acceptance criteria, split two large stories and review the set with an engineer.
days.deliverable: PRD and a set of user stories
checks: The PRD covers problem, goals, scope, non-goals and success measures
Engineer questions are answered in the revised stories
objectives: Write user stories with acceptance criteria

days.topic: Prioritisation Methods: RICE, MoSCoW and Kano
subtopics: Why prioritisation is a product manager's core job
days.lab_task: Score ten candidate features with RICE, classify five with a Kano survey, combine the results into a ranked list and write the reasons for the top three.
days.deliverable: Scored and ranked feature list with reasons
checks: RICE scores use stated reach, impact, confidence and effort
Kano categories come from survey responses
The top three priorities have written reasons

days.topic: Roadmaps: Outcome-Based Roadmaps and Communicating Them
subtopics: Feature roadmaps compared with outcome roadmaps
days.lab_task: Turn a feature list into a now-next-later outcome roadmap for your course product, make versions for executives and engineers, and present it to role-played stakeholders.
days.deliverable: Outcome roadmap in two versions
checks: Each roadmap item states an outcome
Later items have lower date precision than now items
The two versions suit their audiences

days.topic: Working with Engineering: Estimation, Trade-offs and Technical Debt
subtopics: Technical debt and why it matters to product
days.lab_task: Run a refinement session with role-played engineers, agree estimates and a trade-off for a deadline, and add two technical debt items to the roadmap with reasons.
days.deliverable: Refined backlog, trade-off decision and debt items
checks: Stories have estimates and open questions resolved
The decision states what was cut or delayed and why
Debt items have business impact stated

days.topic: Working with Design: Wireframes, Prototypes and Usability Tests
subtopics: The product manager's role in design
days.lab_task: Review a user flow and Figma prototype for the chosen problem, run two usability tests with a script and agree three changes with the designer.
days.deliverable: Test script, test notes and agreed changes
checks: Both tests have tasks with success recorded
Feedback describes user problems, not preferred solutions
Three changes are agreed with the designer

days.topic: Product Metrics: North Star, Inputs and Guardrails
subtopics: Input metrics that teams can move
days.lab_task: Build a metrics tree for your course product with a north star, three input metrics and two guardrails, and write a precise definition for each.
days.deliverable: Metrics tree with definitions
checks: The north star reflects customer value
Each input metric plausibly drives the north star
Every metric has a formula and a data source

days.topic: Product Analytics: Events, Funnels and Retention
tools: Amplitude, Mixpanel or Google Analytics demo data
days.lab_task: Write a tracking plan for a feature, analyse a funnel and a retention cohort in sample data, and present two findings with a recommendation.
days.deliverable: Tracking plan, analysis and findings
checks: Events have names, properties and triggers
The largest funnel drop-off and a retention pattern are identified
Each finding leads to a recommendation

days.topic: Experiments and A/B Testing in Practice
days.lab_task: Design an A/B test for a feature change with a hypothesis, metrics and sample size, read the results from a sample data set and write the decision.
days.deliverable: Experiment design, results reading and decision
checks: The hypothesis states change, expected effect and reason
Sample size is calculated for the stated effect
The decision follows from the results and guardrails

days.topic: Launching Features: Go-to-Market Checklists and Release Notes
subtopics: Launch tiers by size and risk
Internal enablement for sales and support
days.lab_task: Plan the launch of a feature with a tier, checklist, gradual rollout, release notes and support briefing, and define launch metrics and a rollback trigger.
days.deliverable: Launch plan with release notes and rollback trigger
checks: The checklist covers product, support, sales and marketing
Notes explain the benefit in customer language
A rollback trigger is linked to a metric

days.topic: Stakeholder Management for Product Managers
days.lab_task: Map stakeholders for your course product, handle three role-played feature requests including one from an executive and set up a monthly stakeholder update.
days.deliverable: Stakeholder map, request responses and update template
checks: Each stakeholder has influence, interest and needs
Declined requests are explained with evidence and alternatives
The update template covers progress, decisions and asks

days.topic: Agile Delivery for Product Managers: Backlogs, Sprints and the Product Owner Role
subtopics: Product manager and product owner roles
days.lab_task: Order a backlog for the next two sprints, set sprint goals, run a role-played sprint review and update the backlog from the feedback.
days.deliverable: Ordered backlog, sprint goals and review notes
checks: Items are ordered by value and dependencies
Each sprint has a single clear goal
Review feedback leads to backlog changes

days.topic: Pricing and Packaging Decisions
days.lab_task: Propose a three-tier package for your course product based on willingness-to-pay research and competitor prices, and write the pricing page summary.
days.deliverable: Pricing proposal and pricing page summary
checks: Price points are supported by willingness-to-pay data
Tiers have clear differences in value
The pricing page summary is clear to a new customer

days.topic: Product Management Tools: Jira, Figma and Analytics in a Week of Work
subtopics: Jira or Azure Boards for backlogs and roadmaps
days.lab_task: Simulate a product manager's week with the course tools: refine a backlog, review a design, check a dashboard, record a decision and process customer feedback.
days.deliverable: Week log with tool outputs
checks: The backlog shows refined and ordered items
A decision is recorded with context and reasons
Feedback items are tagged and linked to problems

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Problem-to-Feature Case from Discovery to Launch Plan
days.lab_task: Take your course product from customer interviews to a launch plan: present the evidence, problem statement, PRD, prioritised stories, metrics and launch plan to a stakeholder panel.
days.deliverable: Product case pack and presentation
checks: The problem is supported by interview and data evidence
Stories, metrics and launch plan are consistent with the PRD
The panel approves the plan or sets specific conditions
objectives: Go from problem to launch plan

intermediate.summary: For product managers with one to three years of experience who own a product area. Covers continuous discovery, opportunity solution trees, assumption testing, product strategy, outcome OKRs, cost of delay, experiment design, retention and growth loops, product-led growth, monetisation, B2B and platform products, product operations, technical fluency, product debt, go-to-market, customer success feedback, data-informed decisions and AI features.
prerequisites: Has worked as a product manager or product owner for at least a year
Writes requirements and prioritises a backlog
outcomes: Run continuous discovery and test assumptions before building
Set product strategy and outcome OKRs for an area
Design experiments and drive retention, growth and monetisation
Work across engineering, marketing, sales and support to deliver outcomes

days.topic: Continuous Discovery Habits: Weekly Customer Contact
subtopics: Discovery as a weekly habit, not a phase
The product trio: product, design and engineering
Sharing discovery with the wider team
Discovery in B2B and regulated settings
days.lab_task: Set up a weekly interview cadence for your product area with automated recruiting, run two interviews as a trio and write interview snapshots that the team can use.
days.deliverable: Discovery cadence plan and two interview snapshots
checks: The plan schedules at least one interview each week
Product, design and engineering take part in both interviews
Snapshots capture opportunities in a reusable format

days.topic: Opportunity Solution Trees and Assumption Mapping
subtopics: Desired outcome at the top of the tree
Desirability, viability, feasibility and usability assumptions
Assumption mapping by importance and evidence
Picking the riskiest assumptions to test
Updating the tree as you learn
days.lab_task: Build an opportunity solution tree for a product outcome, choose one opportunity with reasons, map assumptions for three solutions and pick the two riskiest to test.
days.deliverable: Opportunity solution tree and assumption map
checks: Every opportunity connects to the desired outcome
At least three solutions are considered for the chosen opportunity
The two chosen assumptions are high importance and low evidence

days.topic: Testing Assumptions: Prototypes, Fake Doors and Concierge Tests
subtopics: Fake door and painted door tests
Concierge and Wizard of Oz tests
Deciding to build, change or stop
days.lab_task: Design and run two assumption tests with written success criteria (for example a prototype test and a fake door), and decide whether to build, change or stop the solution.
days.deliverable: Two test cards, results and a decision
checks: Success criteria are written before the test runs
Both tests produce evidence against the criteria
The decision follows from the evidence

days.topic: Product Strategy: Where to Play and How to Win
subtopics: Strategy kernel: diagnosis, guiding policy, actions
Linking strategy to roadmap and OKRs
days.lab_task: Write a one-page product strategy for your area with a diagnosis, target segment, advantage and three bets, and test it by deciding between two roadmap options.
days.deliverable: One-page product strategy and option decision
checks: The strategy says which customers and problems are not targeted
The diagnosis names the key challenge with evidence
The strategy decides between the two options

days.topic: Outcome-Based OKRs for Product Teams
subtopics: Key results that measure behaviour change
Common OKR mistakes in product teams
days.lab_task: Write quarterly OKRs for your product team that measure customer behaviour, link them to the strategy and metrics tree, and run a mid-quarter check-in with sample data.
days.deliverable: Team OKRs and a check-in report
checks: No key result is a feature delivery
Each objective links to the strategy
The check-in reports progress and confidence for each key result

days.topic: Advanced Prioritisation: Cost of Delay and Opportunity Scoring
subtopics: CD3: cost of delay divided by duration
Opportunity scoring from importance and satisfaction
Portfolio balance: growth, retention and debt
days.lab_task: Calculate cost of delay and CD3 for eight initiatives, score opportunities from survey data, build a balanced quarter plan and explain one priority change to stakeholders.
days.deliverable: Prioritised quarter plan with calculations
checks: Cost of delay and CD3 are calculated with stated assumptions
The plan includes growth, retention and debt work
The priority change is explained with the new evidence

days.topic: Experiment Design: Hypotheses, Sample Size and Pitfalls
subtopics: Experiment design beyond simple A/B tests
days.lab_task: Review three flawed experiment designs, fix each one, design a new experiment with power and minimum detectable effect, and write a readout from sample results.
days.deliverable: Fixed designs, new experiment design and readout
checks: Each flawed design has its main problem identified
The new design states power and minimum detectable effect
The readout states result, confidence and decision

days.topic: Retention, Engagement and Growth Loops
days.lab_task: Find the activation moment in sample data, map one growth loop for your product and design two retention experiments with metrics.
days.deliverable: Activation analysis, growth loop map and experiment designs
checks: The activation moment is supported by cohort data
The loop shows input, action, output and reinvestment
Each experiment targets a retention metric

days.topic: Product-Led Growth and Onboarding
subtopics: Free trials, freemium and reverse trials
days.lab_task: Map the current onboarding of a product, measure time to value from sample data, redesign the first-run experience and define product-qualified lead criteria.
days.deliverable: Onboarding map, redesigned flow and PQL criteria
checks: Time to value is calculated from data
The new flow removes at least two steps before first value

days.topic: Pricing Strategy and Monetisation Experiments
subtopics: Monetisation models: subscription, usage, transaction and ads
Van Westendorp and conjoint in brief
days.lab_task: Choose a value metric for your product, design a price test, analyse sample willingness-to-pay data and recommend a change with expected revenue impact.
days.deliverable: Value metric choice, price test design and recommendation
checks: The metric grows with customer value
The test design controls for segment and timing
Revenue impact is estimated with assumptions

days.topic: B2B Product Management: Buyers, Users and Enterprise Requirements
subtopics: Buyers, users and influencers in B2B
Enterprise requirements: security, compliance and integration
days.lab_task: Map buyers and users for an enterprise deal, evaluate three large-customer requests against strategy, and plan a customer advisory board session.
days.deliverable: Account map, request evaluations and advisory board plan
checks: Buyers, users and influencers are identified with needs
Each request is accepted, adapted or declined with reasons
The agenda focuses on problems, not feature voting

days.topic: Platform and API Products
subtopics: API design decisions from a product view
days.lab_task: Map the developer journey for an API product, find three friction points, propose a versioning and deprecation policy and define platform metrics.
days.deliverable: Developer journey map, policy and metrics
checks: The map runs from discovery to first successful call
The policy covers versions, notice periods and support
Metrics include time to first call and active integrations

days.topic: Product Operations: Feedback Systems and Insights
subtopics: Feedback intake from sales, support and users
Tagging and linking feedback to problems
days.lab_task: Design a feedback system with intake channels and tags, process fifty sample feedback items and produce a monthly insight report for leadership.
days.deliverable: Feedback system design and an insight report
checks: All channels feed one system with tags
Items are tagged and linked to problems
The report ranks problems by frequency and impact

days.topic: Technical Fluency for Product Managers: Architecture, APIs and Data
subtopics: How web and mobile systems fit together
days.lab_task: Read an architecture diagram with an engineer, trace one user action through the system, make an API call with Postman and estimate the cloud cost of a new feature.
days.deliverable: Annotated diagram, traced flow and cost estimate
checks: The user action is traced through each component
A request and response are explained in plain terms

days.topic: Managing Product Debt and Quality Trade-offs
days.lab_task: Build a debt register for a product area with costs, set an error budget with engineering and add a debt reduction theme to the roadmap with a business case.
days.deliverable: Debt register, error budget and roadmap theme
checks: Each debt item has an estimated cost or risk
The error budget is agreed with engineering
The business case explains the value of the debt work

days.topic: Go-to-Market with Marketing and Sales: Positioning and Enablement
days.lab_task: Write a positioning statement and messaging for two segments, build a battle card and run a role-played sales enablement session for a new feature.
days.deliverable: Positioning, messaging, battle card and enablement notes
checks: The statement names target, category, benefit and difference
The battle card covers objections and competitor comparisons
Role-played sellers can explain the feature value

days.topic: Customer Success and Support Feedback Loops
subtopics: What support and success teams know
days.lab_task: Analyse a month of support tickets for themes, define a customer health score with customer success, and write a close-the-loop message for customers whose problem was fixed.
days.deliverable: Ticket analysis, health score and close-the-loop message
checks: Top ticket themes are ranked by volume and impact
The health score uses product and support signals
The message tells customers what changed

days.topic: Data-Informed Decisions: Dashboards, Cohorts and Causality
subtopics: Data literacy for the product team
days.lab_task: Build a product dashboard for weekly reviews, analyse a cohort question from sample data, find one misleading correlation and record a decision with its evidence.
days.deliverable: Dashboard, cohort analysis and decision record
checks: Each dashboard chart links to a decision or owner
The decision record cites data and research

days.topic: AI Features: Use Cases, Evaluation and Responsible Design
days.lab_task: Choose an AI use case for your product, prototype it with an LLM playground, build a twenty-case evaluation set, measure quality and design the fallback and user messaging.
days.deliverable: AI use case, prototype results, evaluation and design notes
checks: The use case explains why AI fits the problem
Quality is measured on the evaluation set
Fallbacks and user messages handle failures

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Discovery-to-Delivery Plan for a Growth Opportunity
days.lab_task: Choose a growth opportunity, take it from outcome to opportunity tree, run two assumption tests, design the experiment and go-to-market plan and present it to role-played product leadership.
days.deliverable: Discovery-to-delivery plan and presentation
checks: The plan links to strategy and OKRs
Assumption tests support the chosen solution
Leadership approves the plan or sets specific conditions

advanced.summary: For senior product managers, group product managers and heads of product. Covers leading product managers, portfolio strategy, multi-year vision, product organisation design, business models and unit economics, AI-native products, platform strategy, pricing at scale, international expansion, rationalising products after acquisitions, executive reviews, metrics and experimentation platforms, regulation and trust, sunsetting, new bets, hiring and career ladders, product culture, competitive response and investment cases.
prerequisites: Has owned a product or product area for several years
Leads other product managers or a significant product line
Takes part in business planning and investment decisions
outcomes: Set portfolio strategy and multi-year vision across products
Design product organisations, career ladders and an empowered product culture
Make business model, pricing, platform and investment decisions with evidence
Lead products through regulation, competition, acquisitions and retirement

days.topic: Product Leadership: Leading Product Managers and Product Teams
subtopics: From product manager to product leader
Setting context instead of making every decision
Managing up and across the executive team
Your weekly rhythm as a product leader
days.lab_task: Run a role-played product review that coaches rather than directs, hold a coaching one-to-one with a struggling product manager and design your weekly leadership rhythm.
days.deliverable: Review notes, coaching notes and leadership rhythm
checks: Most leader contributions in the review are questions
The one-to-one ends with development actions
The rhythm includes reviews, coaching and strategy time

days.topic: Portfolio Strategy Across Multiple Products
subtopics: Portfolio views: lifecycle, growth and investment
days.lab_task: Analyse a portfolio of five products, propose an investment allocation across core, adjacent and new bets and recommend one product for reduced investment.
days.deliverable: Portfolio analysis and allocation proposal
checks: Each product has lifecycle, growth and margin data
The allocation follows the stated strategy

days.topic: Building Product Vision and Multi-Year Strategy
subtopics: Vision for three to five years
Linking long-term vision to annual plans
days.lab_task: Write a six-page strategy narrative for a product line with a three-year vision, scenarios, themes and capability plan, and review it with role-played executives.
days.deliverable: Strategy narrative and review notes
checks: The narrative covers scenarios for three years
Themes connect to the next year's plan
Executive questions are answered in the revised narrative

days.topic: Product Organisation Design: Team Topologies and Ownership
subtopics: Organising teams by customer, product or capability
Ratio of product managers to engineers
days.lab_task: Map the teams and dependencies of a case product organisation, design a new team structure that reduces dependencies and plan the transition.
days.deliverable: Current map, new design and transition plan
checks: The new design cuts dependencies for key outcomes
The plan covers people, ownership and timing

days.topic: Business Models and Unit Economics
subtopics: Unit economics for marketplaces and platforms
days.lab_task: Build a unit economics model for a case product, find the weakest metric and propose two product changes with their expected effect on payback.
days.deliverable: Unit economics model and improvement proposal
checks: CAC, LTV, margin and payback are calculated
The weakest metric is identified with evidence
Each proposal states its expected effect

days.topic: Building AI-Native Products: Models, Data and Evaluation at Scale
subtopics: Choosing models: hosted, open and fine-tuned
Cost and latency management at scale
days.lab_task: Write a strategy for an AI-native product covering model choice, data feedback loops, evaluation gates, cost model and safety plan, and defend it to a role-played review board.
days.deliverable: AI product strategy and review notes
checks: The model choice compares quality, cost and control
Evaluation gates are defined before release
The safety plan covers abuse and red teaming

days.topic: Platform Strategy and Ecosystems
days.lab_task: Map the ecosystem for a case platform, identify its network effects, design a partner programme and define ecosystem health metrics.
days.deliverable: Ecosystem map, partner programme and health metrics
checks: The map shows participants and value flows
The partner programme states benefits, rules and tiers
Health metrics cover supply, demand and quality

days.topic: Pricing at Scale: Tiers, Usage-Based Pricing and Price Changes
days.lab_task: Redesign the pricing architecture of a case product to include usage-based pricing, model revenue and churn effects and plan the migration of existing customers.
days.deliverable: Pricing architecture, model and migration plan
checks: Tiers and usage metrics align with customer value
Revenue and churn effects are modelled with scenarios
The plan covers communication and grandfathering

days.topic: International Expansion and Localisation of Products
subtopics: Payments, tax and regulation by country
days.lab_task: Score four candidate countries for expansion, choose one, write the localisation checklist and launch plan, and define success measures for the first year.
days.deliverable: Market scoring, localisation checklist and launch plan
checks: The choice is supported by the scoring model
The checklist covers language, payments, regulation and support

days.topic: Product Rationalisation After Acquisitions
days.lab_task: Analyse two overlapping products after a case acquisition, decide what to keep, merge or retire, and write the customer migration and communication plan.
days.deliverable: Overlap analysis, decision and migration plan
checks: Revenue, customers and capabilities are compared
The decision is justified for customers and the business
The migration plan includes timing and support

days.topic: Executive Reviews for Product Leaders: Strategy Updates and Board Reporting
days.lab_task: Prepare and deliver a quarterly business review for a product line with outcome progress, an investment ask and one piece of bad news, then handle challenge from a mock executive team.
days.deliverable: QBR deck and review notes
checks: The investment ask has expected return and risks

days.topic: Metrics Trees and Experimentation Platforms at Scale
days.lab_task: Build a company metrics tree with owners, design an experimentation programme with holdouts and guardrails, and write metric governance rules.
days.deliverable: Metrics tree, experimentation programme and governance rules
checks: Every metric in the tree has an owner team
Rules cover definitions, changes and reviews

days.topic: Regulation, Privacy and Trust in Product Decisions
subtopics: Regulations affecting products: GDPR, India's DPDP Act and sector rules
days.lab_task: Run a privacy impact assessment for a new data-driven feature, check accessibility requirements, and plan product changes for an upcoming regulation.
days.deliverable: Privacy assessment, accessibility check and regulatory plan
checks: Data flows, risks and mitigations are documented
The plan has deadlines and owners

days.topic: Sunsetting Products and Features
subtopics: When to retire a product or feature
days.lab_task: Decide whether to sunset a low-usage feature from case data, write the sunset plan with notice, migration and communication, and define how success will be measured.
days.deliverable: Sunset decision and plan
checks: The decision uses usage, revenue and cost data
The plan covers notice, migration and support

days.topic: Finding Product-Market Fit for New Bets
subtopics: Sean Ellis survey and retention signals
Small, fast teams for new bets
Protecting new bets from the core business
days.lab_task: Evaluate a case new bet against product-market fit signals, decide whether to fund, pivot or stop it using kill criteria, and write the next stage plan.
days.deliverable: Fit evaluation, decision and next stage plan
checks: Survey and retention signals are analysed
The decision applies criteria set in advance
The plan has goals and funding for the next stage

days.topic: Hiring, Coaching and Career Ladders for Product Managers
days.lab_task: Write a product manager career ladder with competencies by level, design an interview loop with an exercise and assess two sample candidates.
days.deliverable: Career ladder, interview loop and candidate assessments
checks: The loop tests discovery, delivery and communication
Candidates are assessed against the same criteria

days.topic: Product Culture and Operating Model: Empowered Teams
subtopics: Feature teams compared with empowered product teams
Decision rights between product, design and engineering
Changing culture in a sales-led company
days.lab_task: Assess the product operating model of a case company, design a target model with empowered teams and decision rights, and plan the culture change.
days.deliverable: Assessment, target operating model and change plan
checks: The target model defines planning, decisions and rituals
The plan has phases and measures

days.topic: Competitive Strategy and Responding to Disruption
subtopics: When to fast follow and when to differentiate
days.lab_task: Run a war game where a competitor launches a cheaper AI-based alternative, choose your response and write the product and go-to-market changes.
days.deliverable: War game notes and response plan
checks: The competitor's likely moves are mapped
The response protects core customers and builds advantage
Product and go-to-market changes have owners and dates

days.topic: Product Investment Cases and Due Diligence
subtopics: Product due diligence on acquisition targets
days.lab_task: Prepare an investment case comparing build, buy and partner options for a new capability, including product due diligence on one acquisition target, and present it to a mock investment committee.
days.deliverable: Investment case, due diligence report and committee outcome
checks: Build, buy and partner are compared on cost, time and risk
Due diligence covers product, technology and customers
The committee approves an option or sets conditions

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Product Strategy and Operating Plan for a Business Line
days.lab_task: Lead a business line in a detailed case: write the product vision and portfolio strategy, the economics, the organisation and operating model and the investment asks, and present them to a mock executive committee.
days.deliverable: Product strategy pack and executive presentation
checks: Vision, portfolio and economics are consistent
The operating model supports the strategy
The committee approves or sets specific conditions
objectives: Lead strategy for a business line
